Error.description:
Why a command was refused, or a problem it found, in Silico's error contract: a code, a
message, and, where they apply, the feature, the elements at fault (the first of them, and
how many in all), the request's field at fault, the cause, what to do, and the names that
might have been meant. Every field is always present: null, or empty, where it doesn't
apply.

candidates.description: What might have been meant, such as the names nearest one that found nothing.

cause.description: What lay under it, such as the kernel's own failure, if known.

code.description: What kind of error it is: one of Silico's error codes, such as `invalid_input`.

elements.description: The elements at fault, by name: the first of them, if there are many.

elements_total.description: How many elements are at fault, listed or not.

feature.description: The ID of the feature at fault, if one is.

message.description: What went wrong, in a sentence.

parameter.description: The field at fault, as a dotted path (`position.2`), if one is.

suggestion.description: What to do about it, if Silico can say.

fault.description: The kernel fault the model's rebuild met, if it met one: null if none.

revision.description: The revision the model was rebuilt from.

ModelOf.description:
Which model was read: the session's current revision's (`current`), or the newest one
published (`published`), which may be an older revision's.

Ran.description: A command that ran: `ok` is true, and `result` is the command's own result.

model.description: The model the command read: null if it read none.

result.description: The command's result, as the command's own schema gives it.

session.description: The session as the command left it: null for a command that takes no session.

Refused.description:
A command refused, or one that couldn't run: `ok` is false, and `errors` gives every
reason, in the order found.

errors.description: The reasons, in the order found: the first 100.

model.description: The model the command read: null if it read none.

session.description:
The session as the command left it: null for a command that takes no session, or a
session that isn't open.

total.description: How many reasons there are, listed or not.

Session.description: The session as the command left it.

id.description: The session's ID, `s1`, `s2`, ...: give it in each request to the session.

path.description: The document's path, as `open` was given it.

reloaded.description:
Whether the session read its file again before the command, finding it changed on
disk.

revision.description: The session's revision: 1 at `open`, and one more for each change to its document.

description:
Every command's response: one that ran, or one refused. Every field is always present,
null where it doesn't apply.
title: Response
